messages:
alex: FYI — Acme reported that Structured JSON mode (streaming) produced invalid JSON, breaking their downstream parser. They see 400s (parse error) + client retried which spiked latency.
mina: Can you paste a repro and request-id?
alex: Repro from their side (sanitized): 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-v2\",\"mode\":\"structured\",\"stream\":true,\"prompt\":\"...\"}'
```
Their client receives stream chunks; one chunk contains: 
```json
{\"content\":\"This is a string with an unescaped newline\nand a lone backslash \\\\ at the end\"}
```
That leads to parser error: \"invalid character '\\n' in string literal\" and our logs show: parser.go:123: unexpected end of JSON input
jordan: Hmm looks like chunk boundary split a surrogate pair or escaped sequence. If stream chunk splits a \\uD83D surrogate, the UTF-8 becomes invalid when concatenated early.
alex: Request-IDs: req_0a1b2c3d / req_4f5e6g7h. Logs:
```
ERROR: structured-parser: request=req_0a1b2c3d parse_error=\"unexpected end of JSON input\" client_ip=...
WARN: stream-reassembler: dropped byte 0x00 at boundary
```
sam: Any signs of auth or billing hits?
alex: Customer hit repeated retries -> we saw a couple 429s from their IP. Billing doesn't seem broken but they got alerts for overages from retries. No auth failures.
support-bot: Alert: structured-json-parse-errors increased 8x in the last hour.
mina: Short-term workaround: ask customer to set stream=false or to buffer full response before parsing. Also they can add a small regex to detect unclosed quotes and retry the call.
jordan: Long term: runtime should ensure we never emit half-surrogates or split escape sequences across chunks; either emit safe chunk boundaries or emit replacement escapes (\\uXXXX). I'll open ENG-RUNTIME ticket with reproducible trace.
alex: I'll prepare a minimal reproducer and attach request ids + sample stream. Escalating to eng-runtime, cc @jordan @mina. :pray:
sam: Thanks — I'll add SRE oncall to monitor latency and rate spikes.
